subject: Media Literacy
title: Left-Leaning Bias in Media
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Left-Leaning Bias in Media.

hook.text: Surveys show journalists in the US are more likely to identify as liberal than conservative. Does that affect coverage?

buildup.text: Left-leaning bias manifests in story selection, framing, and source choices that favor progressive perspectives.

discovery.text: Outlets like MSNBC and The Guardian have editorial stances that lean left, which shapes their coverage angles.

twist.text: Liberal media bias is real in some outlets — but it doesn't mean all mainstream media leans left uniformly.

climax.text: Recognizing left-leaning bias means noticing which progressive assumptions go unquestioned in certain coverage.

punchline.text: Left bias exists. It's not everywhere. Learn to spot where it is.

quiz.question: How does left-leaning bias typically manifest in news?
options: Through story selection, framing, and source choices favoring progressive perspectives
